description_good_justification: README.md line 3 gives a one-line tagline ('C2PA manifest embedding and hard binding for unstructured text using Unicode variation selectors') and the Overview section explains what the software does and why.
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (repo root, discoverable from the GitHub repo page) explains how to obtain the code (git clone), report issues, and contribute (fork, branch, PR). SECURITY.md covers vulnerability feedback. README.md itself does not link to CONTRIBUTING.md, which is a gap, but the file is present and standard-location.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section documents the process: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and Conventional Commits style for commit messages.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; both are FLOSS licenses.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both MIT and Apache License 2.0 are OSI-approved licenses (confirmed via LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE file contents at repo root).
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md (9.0K) documents installation, zero-dependency design, embed/extract usage, hard-binding usage, deterministic padding, and error handling, with runnable code examples.
documentation_interface_justification: Public API is documented via rustdoc (src/lib.rs:95 #![warn(missing_docs)] enforces doc coverage), published to docs.rs (badge in README.md), and README.md gives worked examples of wrapper::embed/extract/strip and hardbinding::compute_data_hash/verify_data_hash inputs and outputs.
sites_https_justification: All project sites are HTTPS-only: github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text, crates.io, docs.rs, npmjs.com, pypi.org (see README badges and install instructions).
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text --jq .has_issues returned true), publicly readable and searchable, URL-addressable, and open to any GitHub user with no proprietary client required.
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and all code comments/doc comments observed are in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows commits through 2026-08-22 (docs commit) and merged dependency PRs through 2026-08-24 (PR #9), within the last 60 days of today (2026-08-26); v0.2.0 was tagged 2026-08-02.
repo_public_justification: gh repo view reports isPrivate:false; the repo is publicly readable at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text.
repo_track_justification: git is used; `git log --format='%ad %an %s'` shows author, date, and message for every commit.
repo_interim_justification: Multiple non-release commits exist between the v0.1.0 (2026-07-31) and v0.2.0 (2026-08-02) tags, and further commits (e.g. a1a77aa, 3361b58) exist after v0.2.0 with no new tag yet.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses git, a distributed VCS.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version field (0.2.0) plus git tags (v0.1.0, v0.2.0) give each release a unique, unambiguous identifier.
version_tags_justification: `git tag` lists v0.1.0 and v0.2.0; `gh release list` confirms matching GitHub releases dated 2026-07-31T18:59:44Z and 2026-08-02T15:31:31Z.
release_notes_justification: The GitHub release for v0.2.0 has a body of only '**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0' (verified via `gh release view v0.2.0 --json body`), which is an auto-generated compare link, not human-written release notes. .github/workflows/changelog.yml is supposed to commit a CHANGELOG.md on every push to main, but `gh api repos/.../contents/CHANGELOG.md` returns 404 and no CHANGELOG.md commit appears in `git log`, so no changelog exists either.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No meaningful release notes exist yet (see release_notes) and no publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release, so there is nothing to identify.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml, referenced from CONTRIBUTING.md.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the tracker in use (has_issues:true via gh api).
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: `gh issue list --state all` returns an empty list: no user-filed bug reports exist yet. All tracker/PR activity to date (#1-#10) is automated dependabot dependency bumps, so there is no unacknowledged human report.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Same evidence as report_responses: no enhancement requests have been filed yet (gh issue list is empty), so none are unaddressed.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, permanent, searchable archive of reports and responses at github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text/issues.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md at repo root documents the process: do not use public issues; open a private GitHub Security Advisory or email admin@writerslogic.com. Note: the advisory link in SECURITY.md line 12 (github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/security/advisories/new) points at a different repo (c2pa-zip) rather than c2pa-unstructured-text, a real defect in the doc, but the email channel documented alongside it still works and GitHub's private-advisory feature exists natively on this repo regardless of the wrong link.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explains how to report privately (GitHub Security Advisories or email admin@writerslogic.com). Same broken-link caveat noted in vulnerability_report_process applies to the advisories URL.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received: `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-unstructured-text/security-advisories` returns an empty list, so there is no response-time data for the last 6 months.
build_justification: cargo build/cargo check is the automated build system, run in .github/workflows/ci.yml (check job) and release.yml (verify job).
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, is used (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock); wasm-pack and maturin are the standard tools for the wasm/Python builds respectively.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-pack, and maturin (used in .github/workflows/release.yml) are all FLOSS.
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` is the standard, idiomatic invocation for a Rust crate; CI runs `cargo test --features hard-binding,checksum-v2` (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 57).
test_justification: 48 #[test] functions exist across src/wrapper.rs, src/hardbinding.rs, src/vs.rs, src/error.rs, and tests/vectors.rs (verified by grep -c '#\[test\]'); CONTRIBUTING.md documents `cargo test` as the way to run them.
test_most_justification: 48 tests exercise wrapper encode/decode/padding, hardbinding compute/verify, error codes and is_no_manifest_located, and cross-checked C2PA A.8 spec vectors (tests/vectors.rs). No coverage-percentage tool is used, so breadth is based on function count and module spread, not a measured coverage number.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs check, test, and msrv jobs on every push and pull request to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2: 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features.'
tests_are_added_justification: src/wasm.rs (137 lines, added in commit 42c6ca8 'feat: add WebAssembly bindings and an npm release job') and src/python.rs (165 lines) contain zero #[test] functions (verified by grep), while the core logic they wrap (src/wrapper.rs, src/hardbinding.rs, src/vs.rs, src/error.rs) carries 40 tests between them. The stated test-addition policy was not followed for this binding-layer feature commit.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents 'add tests' as an explicit step in the Submitting Changes process.
warnings_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --features hard-binding,checksum-v2 -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` on every push/PR.
warnings_fixed_justification: `-D warnings` turns every clippy warning into a hard CI failure, so warnings cannot merge to main unresolved.
warnings_strict_justification: src/lib.rs:95 sets #![warn(missing_docs)] and CI runs clippy across --all-targets with multiple feature combinations at -D warnings, which is close to maximal strictness available on stable Rust.
know_secure_design_justification: README.md documents explicit threat-model reasoning: a candidate wrapper that fails to decode beside a valid one is skipped rather than reported, because 'letting stray bytes carrying the magic invalidate an otherwise good wrapper would hand anyone who can append to the text a denial of service.' src/lib.rs:94 sets #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-wide. The checksum-v2 feature (Cargo.toml comments) is explicitly designed to fail safe (reject) rather than decode to wrong bytes on a mangled carrier.
know_common_errors_justification: Same design evidence as know_secure_design, plus supply-chain-focused commits a1a77aa ('ci(security): pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read') and e0620de ('fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29'), and SECURITY.md's supply-chain section (SHA-pinned Actions, Scorecard, Dependency Review, Dependabot), showing applied knowledge of common CI/CD and dependency-vulnerability classes.
crypto_published_justification: src/hardbinding.rs lines 52-59 define Algorithm { Sha256, Sha384, Sha512 } — only publicly published NIST hash algorithms are used.
crypto_call_justification: Hashing is delegated to the RustCrypto `sha2` crate (Cargo.toml dependency) via the injectable Hasher trait, rather than being reimplemented.
crypto_floss_justification: The `sha2` and `unicode-normalization` crates used for the optional hard-binding feature are both FLOSS (MIT/Apache-2.0 licensed on crates.io).
crypto_keylength_justification: The crate computes hashes for hard-binding integrity only; it does not generate, store, or manage cryptographic keys, so key-length requirements do not apply.
crypto_working_justification: The Algorithm enum (src/hardbinding.rs:52-59) only exposes SHA-256/384/512; no MD4, MD5, single-DES, RC4, or Dual_EC_DRBG option exists anywhere in the crate.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or other known-weak algorithm is offered by default or otherwise (same Algorithm enum evidence as crypto_working).
crypto_pfs_justification: The crate has no key-agreement or key-exchange functionality; it only computes/verifies content hashes.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The crate stores no passwords or user credentials.
crypto_random_justification: The crate does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces; it only hashes provided text/manifest bytes.
delivery_mitm_justification: The crate is distributed via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served over HTTPS, and the source repo is cloned over HTTPS/SSH from GitHub.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No plain-HTTP hash-only delivery mechanism is used; all package registries (crates.io, npmjs.com, pypi.org) serve exclusively over TLS with registry-level integrity checks.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open vulnerability reports exist against the project (`gh api .../security-advisories` returns an empty list); commit e0620de ('fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29') shows a prompt dependency-security fix already applied.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported. Dependabot runs weekly (.github/dependabot.yml) and dependency-bump PRs #1-#5 were merged within days of being opened, showing a fast turnaround pipeline is in place for when one is found.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for api key/secret/password/private-key markers found no leaked credentials; the only 'TOKEN' occurrences are `${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}`, `${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`, and `${{ github.token }}` GitHub Actions expressions in .github/workflows/release.yml, which are references to secrets stored in GitHub, not leaked values.
static_analysis_justification: clippy (a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust) runs in .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml on every push, PR, and release tag.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is run with no lint allow-list across --all-targets and multiple feature combinations, which enables clippy's full default lint set, including correctness and suspicious-pattern lints relevant to common bug/vulnerability classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: `-D warnings` promotes every clippy finding to a build failure, so findings cannot merge to main unresolved (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 39-40).
static_analysis_often_justification: ci.yml runs clippy on every push and pull request to main; release.yml re-runs it on every release tag.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing harness, AddressSanitizer/Valgrind job, or other dynamic-analysis tool was found in .github/workflows/ or Cargo.toml.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: src/lib.rs:94 sets #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-wide, so there is no memory-unsafe (C/C++-style) code present to require a memory-safety dynamic tool.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration exists at all (see dynamic_analysis), so no assertion-enabling configuration exists either.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is performed (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
